recent_posts.title: The singularity is ideology not science and it serves concentrated power
recent_posts.summary: A critical examination of the technological singularity narrative, arguing it is more ideological than scientific. Drawing on neuroscience (Damasio, Barrett), philosophy of mind (4E cognition), and political economy (Pasquinelli's analysis of AI as enclosed collective labor), the piece contends that the singularity framing naturalizes the concentration of power in a few private actors while foreclosing democratic accountability. The AI development race is compared structurally to the Cold War nuclear arms race via Dr. Strangelove, where rational actors following self-interest produce collectively catastrophic outcomes. The hopeful counterpoint is that the same human capacities the singularity framework dismisses — embodied relationships, emotional intelligence, social trust, institutional continuity — are precisely what enabled nuclear arms control, and may yet enable meaningful AI governance.

recent_posts.title: Why leaders must resist outsourcing judgment to AI writing tools
recent_posts.summary: Generative AI enables leaders to produce polished, confident-sounding text without doing the hard work of judgment and sensemaking. This accelerates an existing organizational problem where writing became output rather than thinking, and leadership separated from consequence. Real leadership requires staying with raw experience long enough for judgment to form, then deliberately shaping meaning over time with stakes attached. AI can assist with articulation but cannot perform the sequence of feeling what's happening, deciding what it means, and accepting responsibility for the arc that follows. Leaders must choose whether to treat sensemaking as overhead to optimize or as core work that cannot be automated.

recent_posts.title: How AI profits are driving the housing crisis and deepening inequality
recent_posts.summary: AI-driven productivity gains are creating massive profits that flow to capital owners rather than workers, exacerbating a pattern that began in the 1970s when wages stagnated despite rising productivity. These surplus profits increasingly flow into real estate investments, driving up housing costs and deepening inequality. The article argues that without policy intervention, AI will accelerate this cycle, making housing even less affordable while concentrating wealth among property and AI infrastructure owners. Solutions include strengthening worker bargaining power, implementing progressive property taxes, limiting institutional real estate investment, and creating mechanisms for workers to share in AI productivity gains.

recent_posts.title: How AI profits are driving the housing crisis and widening inequality
recent_posts.summary: AI-driven productivity gains are creating massive profits that flow into real estate investments rather than worker wages, exacerbating the housing crisis. Since the 1970s, productivity has grown 72% while worker compensation rose only 12%, creating surplus capital that inflates property values. AI threatens to accelerate this pattern by enabling companies to produce more with fewer workers. The article proposes policy solutions including stronger collective bargaining, progressive property taxes, limits on institutional property purchases, and mechanisms for workers to share in AI-generated profits.

recent_posts.title: AI replaces knowledge workers through economic choice, not technological inevitability
recent_posts.summary: AI is replacing knowledge workers not because it's superior, but because it's cheaper and good enough for business needs. This shift mirrors the Industrial Revolution, where economic incentives drove automation over craftsmanship. Companies are reorganizing around AI tools, affecting engineers, designers, and other tech professionals who were once considered irreplaceable. The key insight is that AI doesn't make autonomous decisions—humans in positions of power choose when and how to deploy it. Rather than panicking or simply adapting, professionals should lead by questioning what systems AI reinforces and designing better alternatives that prioritize human values over pure efficiency.

recent_posts.title: Mindfulness Is Good Business — Startup Patterns
recent_posts.summary: Mindfulness is essential for effective leadership, helping leaders maintain mental clarity, make better decisions, and build stronger teams. Practicing meditation and mindfulness can reduce stress, enhance creativity, and improve overall productivity. Building a regular mindfulness practice leads to long-term benefits for personal well-being and professional success.

recent_posts.title: From Humans Managing Machines To Machines Managing Humans — Startup Patterns
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the ownership rights of newspaper articles and the use of user-generated data by AI builders. It draws parallels between the English Enclosure and the current land grab for data. It also explores the potential impact of AI on knowledge workers and the need for collective action to guide AI development.

recent_posts.title: The Mindful Product Company — Startup Patterns
recent_posts.summary: The future of product development is focused on customer needs, rigorous iteration, and experimentation. Mindfulness is being embraced as a powerful practice to enhance teamwork and creativity within product companies. Startup Patterns has developed a diagnostic tool and forthcoming book, 'The Mindful Product Company,' to help companies integrate modern methods and become more mindful. The tool provides immediate feedback and actionable recommendations, while the book delves deeper into the seven dimensions of mindful product companies. The diagnostic tool can highlight areas of improvement in organizations and promote alignment among teams. It is currently available for free, and taking the survey entitles CEOs or founders to a free strategy session with the Startup Patterns team.

recent_posts.title: STEM Blindness — Startup Patterns
recent_posts.summary: The Paper Ceiling campaign is pushing for more openness to workers with diverse education backgrounds. The initiative caps a decades-long shift in focus away from on the humanities to the technical arts in corporate hiring practices. But an over emphasis on STEM to address the competitive pressures from the global market has also led to a wholesale abandonment of the humanities.

recent_posts.title: Driving your company without a strategy: what can go wrong — Startup Patterns
recent_posts.summary: Most companies have a strategic vision that the whole organization understands. There isn't a communal sense of what the organization is doing and why and how we get there. A lack of a well-defined short and long-term strategy hinders a team's ability to create and execute a product strategy and roadmap.
